instructions.name: accept_prime
docs: The pending prime accepts the role. Two-step so a typo or a
compromised prime alone can never hand over control.

accounts.name: incoming
docs: Must equal config.pending_prime (checked in the handler).

instructions.name: add_operator
docs: Prime adds an operator with role bits (address only — keys stay with
the operator; they sign their own settlement transactions). Rotate by
remove_operator + add_operator with a fresh wallet.

instructions.name: approve_lp
docs: Prime approves an LP wallet for settlement: lock_escrow and release
(by hot roles) only commit to, pay, or credit approved wallets. This
is the one onboarding step a server key can't perform, so a full
server compromise can't settle escrows to an attacker's wallet.

instructions.name: cancel_escrow
docs: User abandons an unfunded escrow: closes the vault ATA and the
account, rent back to the user who paid it. Standard exit property:
nothing a user paid for can stay locked. Stray donations are swept
to the user first so dust can never block the close.

accounts.name: destination_ata
docs: Stray dust destination; must belong to the user.

accounts.name: user
docs: Receives rent from both closed accounts; always the user who paid.

instructions.name: claim_withdraw
docs: The claim's own wallet withdraws credit that has been matured for
LP_SELF_EXIT_DELAY_SECS past the cooldown, without the payout role.
The LP's exit when the platform stops relaying payouts: no role, no
intent (the signature is the LP's), and it works while paused, like
the user's timeout_refund. Destination is still the claim wallet and
the per-mint caps still bound each withdrawal.

accounts.name: claim
docs: The signer's own claim: seeds bind it to the signing wallet.

accounts.name: wallet
docs: The LP itself (claim.wallet).

instructions.name: close_escrow
docs: Platform authority closes a terminal escrow: the (empty) vault ATA is
closed and both accounts' rent returns to the user who paid it.

accounts.name: rent_receiver
docs: Receives rent from both closed accounts; always the user who paid it.

accounts.name: authority
docs: Keeper role or prime (role checked in the handler).

instructions.name: deposit
docs: User funds the escrow vault with the full quoted amount.

instructions.name: initialize_config
docs: One-shot: creates the platform config; the caller becomes prime admin.
Only the program's upgrade authority may call it, so nobody can race
a fresh deployment to claim prime.

accounts.name: prime
docs: Becomes the prime admin. One-shot — the config PDA `init` fails on re-run.
Must be the program's upgrade authority (a fresh deploy can't be raced).

instructions.name: initialize_escrow
docs: Creates the escrow for an order. `order_ref` is the backend's order
reference (sha256 of the public id, e.g. "ord_00000012"); the PDA seed
`order_hash` must equal escrow_order_hash(user, order_ref), so an
escrow address belongs to exactly one depositor and nobody else can
create (squat) it ahead of them.

accounts.name: config
docs: Platform config (read-only); the pause gate on new escrows.

accounts.name: vault
docs: init_if_needed: an ATA for a known escrow PDA can be created by
anyone; with plain init a pre-created vault would block the order.

accounts.name: pool_state
docs: Mint allowlist: escrows exist only for mints prime configured with
set_pool_caps (["pool_state", mint]).

instructions.name: lock_escrow
docs: Platform authority locks the escrow when an LP is assigned and the
fiat leg begins. From this point the user's unilateral timeout refund
is suspended — disputes resolve via platform arbitration (release /
refund), matching the p2p.me FUNDED -> DISPUTED -> RESOLVED model.

accounts.name: authority
docs: Settler role or prime (role checked in the handler).

accounts.name: lp_approval
docs: Prime's approval of the committed LP (["lp", counterparty]).

instructions.name: migrate_claim
docs: Permissionless v1 -> v2 claim migration: the old flat credit becomes
a single fully-matured entry (timestamp 0, so nothing is stranded by
cooldown), the payout nonce survives. Old-layout accounts cannot be
read by this binary, so they pass through here before anything else.

accounts.name: claim
docs: Old flat claim accounts (89 bytes) get the ring layout in place:
their credit becomes one matured entry, nonce/bump preserved.

accounts.name: payer
docs: Pays the realloc rent top-up. Permissionless by design.

instructions.name: migrate_config
docs: Grows the config PDA in place to the current layout: accepts the v1
(LEGACY_LEN) or v2 (LEN_V2) account. New tail bytes arrive zeroed;
from v1 that also zeroes operator roles, so prime re-adds them right
after (deploy runbook). cooldown_secs is always reset to the default.

accounts.name: config
docs: Cannot be a typed Account: the v1 layout is shorter than the new
PlatformConfig and fails deserialization pre-realloc. The handler
verifies seeds, signer, and size from raw bytes.

accounts.name: prime
docs: Prime admin — pays the realloc rent top-up; verified against
config.prime_admin in the handler.

instructions.name: migrate_escrow
docs: Permissionless v1 -> v2 escrow migration: grows the account in place,
legacy prefix preserved, reward_points zeroed. Old-layout accounts
cannot be read by this binary, so open escrows must pass through here
before their next instruction — the backend keeper script runs this
for any open escrow; anyone may pay the rent top-up.

accounts.name: escrow
docs: Cannot be a typed Account: the v1 layout is shorter than the new
Escrow and fails deserialization pre-realloc. Seeds are verified in
the handler from the stored order_hash.

accounts.name: payer
docs: Pays the realloc rent top-up. Permissionless by design.

instructions.name: migrate_pool_state
docs: Prime grows a v1 PoolState in place to the current layout and sets
its outstanding-credit baseline: the sum of all claim credit for this
mint at migration time (read off-chain, asserted by prime). Top-up
cap starts at zero (blocked) until prime sets it.

accounts.name: pool_state
docs: Cannot be a typed Account: the v1 layout is shorter than the new
PoolState and fails deserialization pre-realloc.
the handler.

accounts.name: prime
docs: Pays the realloc rent top-up.

instructions.name: pause
docs: Guardian (or prime) halts all hot-role settlement instructions and
new escrow creation. Asymmetric by design: the pause key travels on
the server for fast incident response; only the cold prime can
unpause. In-flight escrows and the user's timeout backstop are not
affected — pause must never freeze user funds.

accounts.name: authority
docs: Guardian role or prime (checked in the handler).

instructions.name: pool_payout
docs: Payout role settles an LP's claim from the pool vault. Three facts
are enforced here, none by the caller:
- the destination is DERIVED from the claim account's registered
wallet — the payout key cannot name a destination at all
- the amount is the claim's full credit — no amount argument exists
- the LP's own signed intent is verified on-chain (ed25519
precompile + nonce + expiry), so even "patience" payouts of real
claims need a klick the LP themselves made
Intent message (raw bytes, signed by the LP wallet):
b"ZYP2" | program_id[32] | wallet[32] | mint[32] | nonce u64 LE |
first_valid_slot u64 LE
Pays min(matured credit, per-tx cap, window remaining), oldest
credit first; whatever the caps hold back stays matured for the next
payout, so a large claim can never become unpayable.

accounts.name: pool_authority
docs: Pool authority PDA — owns every pool vault and signs payouts only.
A PDA with no lamports is fine: it only ever signs.

accounts.name: claim
docs: The claim being settled — owns the destination by definition.

accounts.name: destination_ata
docs: LP destination, DERIVED from the claim — the caller names nobody.

accounts.name: instructions
docs: Instructions sysvar — the ed25519 intent ix must precede this call.

instructions.name: propose_prime
docs: Prime proposes a successor; the successor must call accept_prime.

instructions.name: refund
docs: Platform authority refunds the vault to the user (cancellation before
fiat from Funded, or resolved appeal in the user's favor from
Processing).

accounts.name: destination_ata
docs: Destination ATA (LP wallet on release, user wallet on refund).

accounts.name: fee_vault_ata
docs: Platform fee recipient ATA — on release, validated to be the prime
admin's token account for this mint. Passed (unused) on refunds.

accounts.name: authority
docs: Settler role (release) or refunder role (refund), or prime — the
right role for the instruction is checked in the handler.

instructions.name: register_claim
docs: Manager role registers an LP's claim account (LP application
approval). Pool-mode releases then credit it on settlement;
without registration, a pool release fails on the missing claim.

instructions.name: release
docs: Platform authority releases the vault to the LP after fiat confirmation.
Requires Processing: release implies the fiat leg happened, which
implies the escrow was locked when the LP was assigned.
Releases to the LP, carving the platform fee out on-chain to the
prime admin's token account. `fee_amount` is asserted by the platform
authority's signature (users never sign release, so they cannot
under-report the fee).
`lp_wallet` is the owner of `destination_ata`: the LP itself (direct
settlement) or the pool PDA (pool mode, where `claimer` names the LP
whose claim is credited).

accounts.name: claim_state
docs: LP claim account — post-settlement credit target in pool mode.
must exist (LP registered) when pool mode credits a claim.

accounts.name: authority
docs: Settler role or prime (role checked in the handler).

accounts.name: lp_approval
docs: Prime's approval of the beneficiary LP (["lp", wallet]).

accounts.name: pool_state
docs: Pool accounting for escrow.mint — outstanding credit grows in pool
mode. Unused in direct mode.

instructions.name: remove_operator
docs: Prime removes an operator (swap-remove; order is not preserved).

instructions.name: revoke_lp
docs: Prime revokes an LP's settlement approval (suspension, wallet
rotation). Takes effect at once: hot roles can no longer lock to,
release to, or credit this wallet. Existing claim credit stays the
LP's and remains withdrawable.

instructions.name: set_cooldown_secs
docs: Prime or the claim manager changes the claim maturity window.
pool_payout enforces it against each entry's own credited_at — no
server is consulted. The manager (a hot key) may only lengthen it, and
not while paused; shortening it matures credit early, so that is
prime's decision alone.

accounts.name: authority
docs: Prime or the claims manager (checked in the handler).

instructions.name: set_max_fee_bps
docs: Prime bounds how much of each escrow a release may cut as fee. Guards
against a compromised settler key starving LP payouts (fee = full
amount would be non-theft but destructive).

instructions.name: set_pool_caps
docs: Prime sets (or tightens) the payout caps for one mint.

instructions.name: set_top_up_cap
docs: Prime caps how much non-settlement credit (top_up_claim) the manager
may post per PAYOUT_WINDOW_SECS for one mint. Zero blocks top-ups.

instructions.name: sweep_surplus
docs: Prime-only profit extraction: moves the pooled spread/surplus to the
treasury ATA. The amount is signer-asserted (recon computes it off-
chain) but bounded on-chain: it may never dip into outstanding claim
credit, so even prime can't sweep LP money. The destination is pinned.
Runs during a pause on purpose — it is part of incident response.

accounts.name: treasury_ata
docs: Treasury — pinned to the prime admin, like every sweep destination.

instructions.name: sweep_vault
docs: Platform authority sweeps residual vault balance (stray donations) to
a platform-owned ATA. Terminal states only; exists so dust can never
permanently block close_escrow (token close requires zero balance).

accounts.name: destination_ata
docs: Sweep destination; must belong to the prime admin (platform treasury).

accounts.name: authority
docs: Keeper role or prime (role checked in the handler).

instructions.name: timeout_refund
docs: User reclaims the vault without platform cooperation:
- Funded: after REFUND_TIMEOUT_SECS since deposit (no LP committed,
so no fiat can be in flight — no double-spend).
- Processing: after PROCESSING_TIMEOUT_SECS since the lock (stalled
platform backstop; the platform owns the LP-loss risk for stalling
past its own settlement SLA).

accounts.name: destination_ata
docs: Refund destination; must belong to the escrow's user.

instructions.name: top_up_claim
docs: Manager role posts non-settlement credits — epoch accruals,
referral claims — so every payout path shares one claim model.
Top-ups move no tokens, so each one must be backed by pool surplus
(vault balance above outstanding credit) and fit the prime-set
per-window top-up cap. A stolen manager key can then only hand out
platform surplus, up to that cap, never LP money.

instructions.name: unpause
docs: Prime clears the pause.

instructions.name: unregister_claim
docs: Manager role removes a claim account (suspension/wallet rotation).
Fails while the account still owes the LP money.

errors.name: InvalidState
errors.msg: escrow is not in the required state for this instruction

errors.name: Unauthorized
errors.msg: signer is not authorized for this escrow

errors.name: InvalidAmount
errors.msg: amount must be greater than zero

errors.name: InvalidDestination
errors.msg: destination token account does not belong to the expected owner

errors.name: TimeoutNotReached
errors.msg: refund timeout has not elapsed since funding

errors.name: OperatorExists
errors.msg: wallet is already an operator or the prime admin

errors.name: OperatorListFull
errors.msg: operator list is full

errors.name: NotAnOperator
errors.msg: wallet is not in the operator list

errors.name: PlatformPaused
errors.msg: platform is paused: hot-role settlement instructions are halted

errors.name: FeeCapExceeded
errors.msg: release fee exceeds the configured max_fee_bps cap

errors.name: PayoutCapExceeded
errors.msg: payout exceeds the per-tx or rolling-window cap for this mint

errors.name: CapsNotSet
errors.msg: pool caps are not set for this mint (prime must call set_pool_caps)

errors.name: InvalidRole
errors.msg: an operator must carry at least one role

errors.name: NotRegistered
errors.msg: claim account is not registered for this wallet

errors.name: CreditNonZero
errors.msg: claim account still owes the LP credit — pay out before unregistering

errors.name: IntentInvalid
errors.msg: payout intent is missing or does not bind this claim and nonce

errors.name: IntentExpired
errors.msg: payout intent is outside its validity window

errors.name: LpNotApproved
errors.msg: LP wallet is not approved on-chain by prime for settlement

errors.name: CooldownDecrease
errors.msg: only prime can shorten the claim cooldown

errors.name: SurplusExceeded
errors.msg: sweep would take outstanding claim credit (only surplus can be swept)

errors.name: TopUpCapNotSet
errors.msg: top-up cap is not set for this mint (prime must call set_top_up_cap)

errors.name: TopUpCapExceeded
errors.msg: top-up exceeds the per-window top-up cap for this mint

errors.name: Underbacked
errors.msg: top-up is not backed: pool vault would hold less than outstanding credit

errors.name: OrderHashMismatch
errors.msg: order hash does not bind this depositor and order reference

fields.name: source
docs: CREDIT_SETTLEMENT (pool-mode release) or CREDIT_TOP_UP.

types.name: ClaimEntry
docs: One credit write with its own timestamp. Maturity is computed per
entry: an entry pays only after config.cooldown_secs has passed since
its credit landed. Time-splitting claims is what lets the chain — not
any server — decide the withdrawable portion.

types.name: ClaimState
docs: One claim account per (LP wallet, mint) — the contract's own knowledge
of who may be paid what. Payout destinations are derived from .wallet;
payout amounts are derived from .entries (never from any argument), so
outflow is structurally always ≤ total credits, and never cooling-fresh.

fields.name: payout_nonce
docs: Replay barrier: every signed payout intent carries this nonce; the
payout bumps it, so a captured intent can never pay twice.

fields.name: locked_at
docs: When the platform locked the escrow for the fiat leg (0 = never).

fields.name: reward_points
docs: Reward-points share of the payment (metadata; 0 for legacy/migrated
escrows and plain-USDC orders). The vault is always `amount` USDC.

fields.name: residual_swept
docs: Stray vault donations swept to the user on cancel (0 normally).

types.name: LpApproval
docs: Prime's on-chain approval of an LP wallet for settlement (PDA, seeds
["lp", wallet]). Hot roles may only commit, pay or credit approved LPs.

types.name: PlatformConfig
docs: On-chain authority registry (PDA, seeds ["config"]). Prime admin manages
the operator set; each operator slot carries role bits and settlement
instructions require the matching role. Prime (a cold multisig) is the
implicit holder of every role: the emergency fallback, never on a server.

fields.name: cooldown_secs
docs: Seconds a claim entry must age before it is withdrawable. Prime-set;
enforced by pool_payout itself, not by anything server-side.

types.name: PoolState
docs: Per-mint pool accounting (PDA, seeds ["pool_state", mint]). Pool custody
lives in ATAs owned by the ["pool"] PDA; this account bounds what the
payout role may move. Zero caps fail closed: payouts block until prime
sets them.

fields.name: window_cap
docs: Rolling payout budget: at most window_cap can be outstanding in
window_used, which drains at window_cap per PAYOUT_WINDOW_SECS.

fields.name: last_payout_at
docs: When window_used was last updated (last payout).

fields.name: outstanding_credit
docs: Sum of all unpaid claim credit for this mint: grows on pool-mode
release credits and top-ups, shrinks on payouts. sweep_surplus may
only take vault balance above it; top-ups must stay below it.

fields.name: top_up_window_cap
docs: Rolling budget for top_up_claim totals, same mechanics as payouts
(prime-set; zero blocks top-ups).
